newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's Seat lost 2,500 cars production for strike.
newsitem.headline: Spain's Seat lost 2,500 cars production for strike.

text.p: Volkswagen's Spanish unit Seat -- hit by a strike in the last two days in its Martorell plant -- has missed production of some 2,500 cars, according to trade union estimates, a spokesman for union CCOO told Reuters.
The strike was called by a minority trade union, CGT, against a pre-agreement signed by workers' commission (CCOO) and the general workers unions (UGT).
The deal is for wage increases to stay in line with Spanish CPI and it established new rules for week-end hours worked.
Trade unions said the strike paralysed production since Monday at midday until this morning, when it was called off.
Next Monday workers will discuss the deal, and CGT, which is looking for a referendum on the issue, is said to be ready to call a new strike, local media said.
It was impossible to confirm immediately the lost production number with the company. The Martorell plant is close to the seaside Spanish city of Barcelona.
